subject: Re: Cerebra – MSA & Order Form: output ownership carveouts and training opt-out
messages:
From: Maya Desai <maya@cerebra.health>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@cerebra.health>
Date: 2028-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA redlines: output ownership + training carveouts

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attaching the MSA with our redlines (see attachment: Cerebra_Redlines_MSAv2.docx). High-level asks from our side:

- Customer retains exclusive ownership of product outputs and derivatives generated by our data/inputs.
- No model retraining or inclusion of our data into vendor models without explicit opt-in.
- A limited feedback license for telemetry/bugfixing only (no training/improvement rights).

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept language that: (a) explicitly prohibits customer data from being used to improve vendor models, and (b) provides a narrow, timeboxed telemetry license for operational troubleshooting. We can be flexible on attribution/marking requirements, but ownership of outputs is non-negotiable for our board.

We'd like to get to a final MSA + order form by the end of next week. Can you route this to legal and let us know a path forward?

Thanks,
Maya

--
Maya Desai
Head of Legal, Cerebra Health

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@cerebra.health>
Date: 2028-04-18T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: output ownership + training carveouts

Maya — thanks for the redlines and the clarity on priorities. Looping in our counsel and commercial lead to align on acceptable language and an execution plan.

Laura / Ben — Cerebra is asking for: 1) explicit customer ownership of outputs/derivatives, 2) a strict training opt-out (no use of their data for model improvement), and 3) a constrained feedback/telemetry license. Attached a one-page summary for legal: mk-ip-summary-for-legal.pdf.

Proposed internal plan:
- Laura: can you propose the narrowest possible legal language that protects us commercially but preserves Redwood's right to operate/monitor (i.e., telemetry for performance & security, not training)?
- Ben: I'll coordinate pricing implications — Cerebra is sized for a Dedicated deployment; if we accept strict training carveouts we may need to add an additional compliance fee or commit to a non-training SLA.

I suggested an optional call on Thursday to resolve open points. Maya/Ari — are you available 4/20 at 10am PT for a 30-min alignment? If not, propose alternatives.

Best,
Markus

--

Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-19T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines: output ownership + training carveouts

Markus / Ben — reviewed Cerebra's redlines and your summary. Quick thoughts and suggested clause language below. I attached inline edits in a redline draft (I will upload final doc to Drive before the call).

Key legal positions I recommend we take:
1) Output ownership: Accept a customer assignment for outputs created exclusively from customer inputs, provided we retain non-exclusive rights to aggregated telemetry for debugging and system improvements where no customer-identifiable content is present. Suggested language: "Customer retains title to Outputs derived solely from Customer Input. Vendor may collect and use aggregated, anonymized telemetry for performance, reliability, and security purposes, and shall not use Customer Input or Outputs to improve or retrain Vendor models absent Customer's written consent."

2) Training opt-out: We can offer a firm opt-out. We should add a representation that we will not use Customer Input/Outputs to train or improve Vendor models, with a carveout for urgent security fixes (operational patches) that do not constitute model training. Suggested language included in attachment.

3) Feedback/telemetry license: Narrow license that allows temporary use of snippets for debugging (e.g., up to 90 days, access restricted to engineering staff, redaction obligations). Consider limiting retention for such telemetry.

Commercial impact: agreeing to a full training opt-out materially impacts our model improvement roadmap; recommend Ben implement either a one-time compliance fee or a committed seat/throughput tier to offset.

I will prepare a tracked-change MSA showing the three elements above. If we accept this posture, we should also harden our operational controls (access logs, restricted retention windows) and produce an audit checklist to share with Cerebra.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Thanks Laura — that language looks sensible. Two commercial notes:

- Pricing: Recommend we present Cerebra with two options in the order form: (A) standard hosted terms with limited telemetry and a training opt-in (lower price), or (B) a dedicated/compliance option with strict opt-out and an added compliance uplift (one-time + higher monthly commit).
- Sales cadence: if they choose (B) we should route to Procurement for a 12-month reserved capacity commit.

I can draft the two order-form bullets and prepare an updated quote once legal locks the MSA language. Confirming I'm on the 4/20 10am PT call.

Ben

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-04-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: output ownership + training carveouts — proposed path forward

Hi Maya/Ari — thanks for the patience while we reviewed. Summary of where Redwood stands and next steps attached (final-redline-msav3.docx). TL;DR:

- Output ownership: Redwood will accept assignment of Outputs generated solely from Customer Input.
- Training: Redwood will include a firm opt-out — Redwood will not use Customer Input or Outputs to train or improve models without written consent.
- Telemetry/Feedback: Redwood requests a narrowly scoped telemetry license for operational debugging and security; retention capped at 90 days and access restricted to named engineering staff.

Commercial note: Because a training opt-out materially limits our product improvement pathways, our standard approach is to move customers who require a full opt-out onto a Dedicated / Compliance price tier with a one-time compliance fee or higher committed monthly spend. Ben will follow up on pricing options in the order form.

If this aligns with Cerebra, please confirm and I'll circulate the tracked MSA for execution and the draft order form with two pricing options. If you want to proceed, sign the attached DocuSign link and we will kick off procurement and onboarding.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Maya: confirm acceptance of the legal positions above (or send targeted redlines).
2) Ben: send 2-option order form and pricing.
3) Laura: finalize redline document and provide audit checklist (access logs + retention proof).

Thanks — happy to discuss on the 4/20 call; otherwise please reply in-thread.

Best,
Markus
